Hi, I'm Calyxa.

A couple weeks ago, Gentlemandrunk graciously accepted my offer to be a moderator here at v/occult When I asked about how heavy a hand was wanted for moderating, it seems that are on the same wavelength regarding post management. When I asked about what I might do about link flair and css, I was told, "you can take this thing and run with it as hard as you want."

I've been running.

I knew only a little css when I was added as moderator. The first thing I did was to create my own test subverse and start tweaking. In working with the code, I grew very unattached to whether or not it stays here on v/occult or not. CSS styling feels very much like a mask which can be put on or changed with relative ease.

After days of polishing, the style appears to be relatively complete and so I have put it here for you all to test drive. I've kept upvote /downvote colors consistent, but changed the shape a little. The night mode toggle is the Light of Hidden Knowledge and the user settings gear icon is replaced with the hexagram of fire and water. Similarly, the water and fire triangles stand in nicely for the V and A in the VOAT logo.

The style covers both day and night modes. As I told Gentlemandrunk, "I'll try not to make it too goth." Day mode is intended to be a parchment manuscript, while night mode has a mossy rock sort of feel.

It is my earnest hope that you all like it and that it doesn't break anything. Any and all feedback welcome! Love it? Hate it? Want just a tweak here or there? Please let me know!

I'd especially like feedback about link flair. I've made space in the style for 7 different flair colors which ought to be more than enough. I've created a 'Meta' flair here already.

The other flairs I used in my test subverse are just a few ides of what might work here.

Personal Project

Experience

Mystery

Query

Recommendation

Academic Resource

Got any favorites from that list? Any ideas or suggestions for alternatives?

If a thread is stickied, its flair on the main list is replaced with the 'Sticky' built-in flair. That said, a 'Group Working' flair is still a fine idea.

In thinking about the new threads from the past few weeks, I am stuck as to which flairs would go on those threads. Particularly the one about that amazing planetarium watch. It's not really a "recommendation," it's more like, "maximum want" or "SHINY!" Both those latter terms are perhaps too pop culture-ish, though. I pondered a "Show and Tell" flair which could be used for photos of work spaces or tools or the like. That's where I went with "Personal Project" instead.

The Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum one could go with either "Academic Resource" (they have a wonderful reading library) or "Recommendation." Of course, "Show and Tell" could work there as well.

"Query" could easily apply to Alias_Unknown's topic and I can see that one being generally useful.

Regarding link colors, Voat's paradigm has always seemed a little "backwards" to me (dull links that get colored brightly after visiting), so that's why I designed this the way I did. The way I learned things from the beginning of web browsers in the mid- to late 1990s was that fresh links ought to be bright and catch the eye while visited links ought to blend in with the rest of the text.

The other thing about links is that there are a TON of them and they're almost all colored individually. I'd installed the style here and discovered that links in post bodies - and only in the dark theme - were still bright purple. Not sure what's up with that, but it's fixed now.

The link locations I'm thinking would be the main targets for color switching are the thread links on the front page of the sub and any links in text posts and replies. I'd like to get a few more opinions on the matter before jumping in and changing that right away, though.

Thank you again for the thoughtful feedback!
